answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This is durable because the trusted grader set only grows through bootstrap capacity, preventing a sudden takeover by a large new flock. This means an attacker must choose: either run a few high-quality identities, or many worthless ones — and neither option beats honest participation. Consider a pulse as the anchor of the cost. A canyon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a river holds the reputation...
